summary: Machine: your laptop, Windows 11, LTspice 26.0.2.1, a separate fresh copy of v0.13.0.
Tests: 367 passed, 13 skipped (those need ngspice), 0 failed. Together with Linux, every one of the 380 tests has now run and passed somewhere.
Commands: 13, longest description 167 characters (the Windows count includes line endings). Under the 200 limit.

Drawings: LTspice turned all 14 drawings back into netlists; all 14 connect exactly the same pins as their source, including the new instrumentation amplifier. My first comparison script misread LTspice's op-amp naming and pin-label comments and wrongly flagged 8; the connections were then checked by hand and the script fixed.
Readability scores are the same as on Linux (LDO 76, buck 69, instrumentation amplifier 27, the rest 99 to 100), so the stale-score finding stands.
Electrical claims: every one repeats in LTspice within 1%, except the LDO load step without the series resistor (59 mV vs 68 mV in ngspice): both say the same thing, a ringing, unstable regulator.

Still running when this version was built: the five templates' tune-and-finish with yield, and the instrumentation-amplifier design, in LTspice. They take about an hour because of the buck converter; this page will be updated when they finish.
